texts: A market runs in the village square every week.
Every distillation requires sea-water from the Salt-bloom Tide-pools.

fields.sentence: A market runs in the village square every week.

review.notes: Indefinite subject with a verbal predicate correctly stays a witness rather than a generic, and the periodic 'every week' takes (Every e 1 week) with no tense atom and no QuantifierPhrase, as the frequency section specifies. Fusing village_square as a classifier compound (genus square, noun modifier not exposed) is a defensible reading of the compound rule, though the possessor/whole 'square of a village' reading is arguably available too.

fields.sentence: Every distillation requires sea-water from the Salt-bloom Tide-pools.

q2_gaps: A multi-word capitalized PLURAL proper name whose head word is a kind word ("the Salt-bloom Tide-pools"): the multi-word-name rule licenses one ordinary type atom read off the kind word inside the name (its example, "the Kestrel River", is singular), while the capitalized-plural-label rule says a plural kind-word label referring as a name is Name-only with no GroupOf and no kind taken from the label word. The instruction set does not say which governs here, nor — if a type atom is licensed — whether a plural-referring name should be typed with the singular kind (Member <name> tide_pool) or by some plural-aware form.
review.notes: Statement 4 (sbtp_type) types the plural-referring name as a single tide_pool, which is the atom the boundary above decides; everything else — the every-rule with Skolem event and dependent sea-water witness, the entity-attached From of origin, the QuantifierPhrase companion, and the sea_water/tide_pool genus atoms — follows the instruction set.
